display_name: Arasaka Tower — Corpo Plaza (lobby and counter-intelligence floor)
why: Arasaka's 620 m Night City headquarters on Corpo Plaza, in the timeline where nothing has been attacked: a public atrial lobby on floor 1 (reception, AIT security checkpoint, guard booths, elevator bank, restrooms, propaganda PA) and the floor-33 counter-intelligence suite where V worked in the corpo lifepath (open-plan bullpen, meeting room, Jenkins' office, AV garage). This proposal restores the two quest sets that own those interiors, their vanilla staff/visitor communities and the lobby's intact look, and leaves the restricted upper tower closed.

open_questions: Floor-33 reachability: the counter-intelligence set is a detached 'fake floor'. Its own device names are q000_dvc_fake_jenkins_floor_fake_lift_terminal_00x and its sectors sit in cells interior_-45_* / -44_*, far from the lobby at interior_-21..-23, and vanilla reaches it only with LiftControllerPS/ForceTeleportToFloor (a scripted ride, not a door action). Confirm on the dev tour whether an enabled #q000_dvc_ara_tow_lift plus authorised floor terminals can actually deliver the player, or whether the owner must accept a populated-but-unreachable floor or add a ride.

Entrance: the lobby's street entrance has no device door in the extracted data (only architecture_prefabFDAU4EA and 15 corporate + 8 guard open-world crowd spawners in loc_arasaka_tower_openworld_prefab2NNNZJA). Verify in game that the front door is open in free roam and that the lobby is walkable before relying on it as the venue's front door.

Security gate: #q000_dvc_arasaka_lobby_security_gate_right is a GenericDeviceControllerPS and its catalogue path is unresolved. Verify it exists (it should be inside the q000_corpo_pr_01_security_gate sub-prefab), that it is unpowered by default, and that the venue spec can add GenericDeviceControllerPS to allowed_device_controllers so ForceON passes --check.

Lift seal: q000_corpo applies DoorControllerPS/ForceSeal to #q000_dvc_ara_tow_lift_door_001. ForceUnlock probably will not clear a seal; confirm and switch to ForceUnseal if the builder/owner allows it.

Community refs: #q000_corpo_com_arasaka_lobby has zero entries in the registry; the entries and spots live in #q000_corpo_com_arasaka_lobby_elevators (nested under #q000_corpo_pr_02_to_elevators). Vanilla's templates point at the parent area anyway. This proposal uses the nested refs that provably own the entries; if the runtime resolves entries only through the area tree, fall back to the parent ref.

Whole-community activation: #q000_corpo_com_arasaka_office_bg is activated by vanilla with empty entry/phase (all entries, initial phase) and is invisible to the catalogue. Confirm the builder supports a wildcard entry for that one item.
Mech exhibit: var_mech_exhibit is on during the prologue and off afterwards. Check on the tour that showing it permanently reads as lobby decor rather than as a left-over scene prop.
Prefab ownership: q000_corpo_02_lizzies_club also declares #q000_corpo_pr_arasaka_office, and cast_and_hubs was not read (brief). Re-check rule 2 at build time for both prefabs.
stripped: venue-node-policy section 4: removed lifepath quest actors Jenkins and Sampson from communities.

Whole-community background crowd for the open-plan counter-intel floor: 39 seated/standing corporate bodies with no-reaction records. Vanilla activates this community with an EMPTY entry name and EMPTY phase name (the catalogue drops that template type), which means 'all entries, initial phase'. The builder needs a wildcard; the phase is 'crowd'.

variant_toggles.why: The lobby's displayed mech: q000_corpo_01 shows it (var_mech_exhibit=1) for the prologue walk through the lobby, and only the wrapper turns it back off afterwards. Our world is 'before anything happened', so the prologue look is the right one; it also matches the wiki's Arasaka ACPA standing guard in the lobby.

Lobby crowd ambience and the ad/screens over the elevators, on by default and switched off only for q115's staged assault. Setting it to 1 makes the 'open for business' state explicit and guards against another phase leaving it muted.

proximity_wait.why: A device entity (the entrance scanner gate) inside #q000_corpo_pr_arasaka_lobby, i.e. exactly where a visitor first meets this venue, so the re-issue of lobby communities and the gate/lift device actions run when the player is actually at the checkpoint rather than at spawn.
